turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right. Scale's done. Weight is three point two four kilograms, temp thirty six point eight. Discharge weight last time was three point five one.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. That's down, isn't it. Umm I've been up half the night worrying about him.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Morning. Ten days old, yellow. When did the colour start?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That's why we're here. His skin's gone yellow, and the eyes. I noticed it six days ago.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja. We thought it was just the light in the room at first.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Feeds?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm breast milk, and then we top up with S26. Every four hours. He sleeps a long stretch at night, which I was happy about, but now I don't know.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wet nappies?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): About six wet ones. And dirty nappies, yellow. Is six enough? I keep counting, sorry.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Six is fine. Any fever?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. He's not hot.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No he doesn't vomit.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough? Working hard to breathe?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. Breathing looks normal.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Blood in the stool?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies. Nothing.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, can I ask, is yellow at ten days still ok? My neighbour's baby got admitted and I'm, umm, spiralling.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll get there. Family history, anything?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Err my father had diabetes in his fifties, my mother did not, and my other sister has pressure but no sugar. My older brother had kidney stones, my younger brother is fine, that's the lot.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): And you, do you work?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja I'm an admin clerk at a hardware shop, hours are eight till half past four, five days. Diet's mostly bread and tea, not much veg since the baby, and exercise, I haven't been out walking at all. Alcohol, I don't drink while I'm breastfeeding, and I don't smoke either. Oh the dog is at my mom's this week, not relevant, sorry.
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Traffic was hectic getting here, hey. Took us forty minutes for what should be fifteen. Anyway.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Medicines for the baby?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the abadek drops. I nearly said point six mils, it's point three mils, once a day, in his mouth. For the vitamins.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything you stopped, or didn't give?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My aunt said gripe water, we never gave it.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Birth weight was three point six, the midwife told us. If that helps.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. I'll look.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sclera are yellow, jaundice down to the chest. Abdomen soft, fontanelle flat, no distress.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Is down to the chest bad? How far is too far? Does he need to stay in today? Sorry, too many questions.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Likely physiological jaundice. Common at day ten. Not confirmed until the bilirubin is back.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): So the blood test, the billy rubin, you'll do it today? Will it hurt?
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Serum bilirubin today. Heel prick. Lab will do it before you leave.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): If it's high, do we stop the breast? Is the formula making it worse? And water, it's warm, does he need water?
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep breastfeeding, formula top up is fine, no water. Feed every two to three hours and wake him. Phototherapy only if the level is high.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok, umm, wait, about the vomiting. Well actually he does bring milk up, a small mouthful after most feeds. I was wrong when I said no.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Since day three. Not the whole feed. He just possets. Sorry.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Green vomit? Blood in it?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No green, no blood.
[SEG0044] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja it's a little spill on the muslin. Not heaps.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that dangerous? Did I cause the yellow by spacing the feeds? What is bilirubin actually doing in him?
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Posseting like that is common, not dangerous. Bilirubin is the yellow pigment. The number is what matters.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): I can take the bloods just now. Heel prick, quick.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Just now, ok. How long for the result? And if he cries, can I feed him straight after?
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Result the same day. Come back in two days. I'll see you here.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days. What if he gets more yellow before that, or won't wake? Do I wait or come in?
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he's floppy, not waking, or the yellow shoots up, come straight in. Otherwise two days.
[SEG0052] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll watch him. I've got time off. Shame, little one.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Thank you, sister. I feel a bit better for asking. We'll do the bloods.

spec.situation: Parents with a ten-day-old baby, yellow skin and feeding every four hours; weight read by the nurse; breast milk plus formula; blood test for bilirubin planned today.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Weight decrease was noted by nurse; patient did not report weight loss as a symptom.
bad.text: weight loss (category=constitutional, status=present, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

Negative finding omitted: no non-bilious vomiting was not sustained after clarification; instead the child has posseting.
Negative finding missing: breathing looks normal (patient-reported).
Family history detail omitted: mother did not have diabetes; younger brother is well.
Medication history omitted: gripe water was never given.
Examination/assessment process detail omitted: bilirubin not confirmed until the result is back.
Investigation detail omitted: bilirubin will be done by heel prick before leaving / same day.
